text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected to pay interim and final dividends in the current year to June 30, 1997, subject to appropriate levels of earnings and cashflow.

"Directors anticipate that, subject to appropriate levels of earnings and cash flow in each of the first and second halves of the 1996/97 financial year, interim and final dividends will be declared and payable from 1996/97 profits," ANI said in announcing its profits for 1995/96.
"However, it is anticipated that any dividend payable in 1996/97 will be unfranked," it said.
Earlier, ANI reported a 78 percent drop in pre-tax operating profit to A$22.99 million and a net loss of A$213.19 million after abnormal losses of A$198.6 million.
The abnormal losses were due largely to the write down of its assets in troubled German environmental engineering unit Holter by A$234 million.
ANI also said it was actively pursuing the possibility of mergers or joint ventures of the Holter businesses.
It said operating cash flows for the year more than doubled to A$169.1 million.
Operating performance in the second half of the financial year improved from core businesses like ANI Aurora, ANI Engineering, ANI Mining Services and Palmer Tube Mills.
"Consolidated operating profit from core operations improved by 20 percent in the second half compared with the first half of the year," it said.
Operating cash flow in the second half of the year trebled to A$130.6 million.
ANI's net gearing ratio rose to 47.5 percent as at June 30, 1996 from 41.1 percent at June 30, 1995, principally due to the Holter writedown. But this ratio had since reduced.

"Following the receipt of the equity component of the Coates Hire sale proceeds and the Cockatoo Dockyard arbritraion damages in August 1996, the net gearing ration has reduced to an estimated 42 percent," ANI said.
ANI did not declare a final dividend for 1995/96, leaving the total dividend at two cents versus nine cents in 1994/95. ANI said its difficulties had been restricted to a few areas.
"The core businesses of ANI, generally, remain strong and offer significant potential for improvement and development notwithstanding competitive pressures," it said.
ANI shares closed unchanged at A$1.02 on Monday.
